title: TraceQA manifest
description: A manifest says which components a page should have. It is YAML on disk (see testbed/sites/buggy-shop/manifest.yaml) and this schema describes the parsed document. `traceqa baseline init` writes one from a run; `traceqa verify --manifest` and the benchmark compare a run with one, by role and name.

ManifestFile.description: The whole manifest. Unknown keys are an error (typo protection): the manifest is the one place in the spec where additionalProperties is false.

formatVersion.description: Absent in older files, which are version 1.

viewports.description: Named viewports, for example desktop and mobile. `hidden` lists these names.

absent.description: Components that must NOT be reported, for example content that only exists after a click.

warnings.description: Warning codes the page is expected to raise.

ManifestAbsent.description: A component that must not be found.

case.description: Which hard case it covers (free text, for reports).

name.description: The accessible name. Absent means an empty name unless template is true.

template.description: True when the instances have different names.

frame.description: Name of the iframe it lives in. Default: the main page.

shadow.description: True when it is inside shadow DOM.

hidden.description: Names of the viewports where it is not visible.

disabled.description: How many instances are disabled. Default 0.

VerifyReport.description: What `traceqa verify --format json` prints: a run checked against a manifest, per target.

manifest.description: The manifest file as it was named on the command line.

strict.description: True when extras (components found but not in the manifest) fail the check.

passed.description: True when no target has a failure.

skipped.description: Targets whose viewport size is not in the manifest.

notes.description: Unused manifest entries and other remarks that do not fail the check.

target.description: The target folder, for example chromium-1280x800.

viewport.description: The manifest's name for the target's viewport.

checked.description: How many manifest components were checked.

severity.description: fail, warning or note. An extra is a warning, or a fail with --strict.

check.description: missing, present, instances, confidence, visible, hidden, disabled, frame, shadow, warning or extra.

message.description: A sentence, with the page's words cleaned and cut.

VerifySkipped.description: A target that was not checked.
